# Temple Scroll Column 51 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all lines in Temple Scroll Column 51 where the three translators significantly diverged, along with SOPHIA's resolution.

---

## 51:1 — "hide yourself" vs. "ignore" vs. "look the other way"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "hide yourself from them" | Literal rendering of Hebrew hit'allamta, reflexive form |
| LOGOS | "ignore them" | Standard English legal equivalent conveying the same obligation |
| PNEUMA | "look the other way" | Idiomatic English capturing the deliberate avoidance |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "ignore" (LOGOS). The Hebrew reflexive "hide yourself" is overly literal in English, while PNEUMA's idiom is too colloquial for legal discourse.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 51:5 — "vessel of a man" vs. "man's garment" vs. "what belongs to a man"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the vessel of a man" | Literal keli gever — "vessel/implement" preserves the Hebrew ambiguity (could include weapons, tools) |
| LOGOS | "a man's garment" | Restructured for clarity; "garment" follows the Deuteronomy tradition |
| PNEUMA | "what belongs to a man" | Broad rendering capturing the wider semantic range of keli |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS phrasing. "Garment" maintains the clothing context evident from the parallel clause while noting that keli may have broader reference.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 51:8 — "parapet" vs. "railing"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "parapet" | Standard architectural term for ma'aqeh |
| LOGOS | "parapet" | Same; universally used in English Bible translations |
| PNEUMA | "railing" | More immediately understood by modern readers |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "parapet" (EMET/LOGOS). This is the standard rendering in all major English translations and accurately describes the ancient Near Eastern architectural feature.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 51:9 — "become holy" vs. "become forfeited" vs. "be ruined"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "become holy" | Literal tiqdash — the mixed crop becomes consecrated/prohibited |
| LOGOS | "become forfeited" | Conveys the practical legal consequence of the sanctification |
| PNEUMA | "be ruined" | Communicates the loss to a modern reader without cultic background |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "become forfeited" (LOGOS). EMET's "become holy" is misleading in English, while PNEUMA's "ruined" loses the cultic dimension. "Forfeited" captures the legal consequence.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 51:11 — "mixed-stuff" vs. "mixed fabric" vs. "two different materials"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "mixed-stuff" | Traditional rendering of sha'atnez as a technical term |
| LOGOS | "mixed fabric" | Clear English equivalent for the textile prohibition |
| PNEUMA | "clothing woven from two different materials" | Explanatory rendering making the prohibition self-evident |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "mixed fabric" (LOGOS). "Mixed-stuff" is archaic, and PNEUMA's expansion is too paraphrastic for the terse legal style.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 51:12 — "twisted-cords" vs. "tassels"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "twisted-cords" | Literal gedilim — emphasizes the physical form |
| LOGOS | "tassels" | Standard translation following most English versions |
| PNEUMA | "tassels" | Same as LOGOS |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "tassels" (LOGOS/PNEUMA). "Twisted-cords" is overly literal; "tassels" is universally recognized.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS/PNEUMA.

---

## 51:14 — "signs-of-virginity" vs. "tokens of virginity" vs. "proof of virginity"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "signs-of-virginity" | Literal betulim with hyphenation to mark construct |
| LOGOS | "tokens of virginity" | Standard scholarly and traditional English rendering |
| PNEUMA | "proof of virginity" | Modern legal language focusing on evidentiary function |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "tokens of virginity" (LOGOS). The traditional rendering preserves cultural specificity without EMET's awkward hyphenation or PNEUMA's modern legal register.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---
